_about: CCL grammar-as-data (C2A2 Command Line v1). Single source of truth for the verb set and the state dimensions each verb writes/reads. Consumed by BOTH the parser (wiki/lib/c2a2-commandline.js) and the janitor drift checks (every verb maps to a declared dimension; every dimension is reachable by >=1 verb; help == this manifest). See wiki/architecture/voice_guide_redesign.md sections 3, 4, 9. Keys beginning with _ are documentation and ignored by consumers.

cursor._note: position within the currently revealed node set; writes through to `selection`, so undo restores the node, not the index

cut._note: The set of nodes allowed to be drawn. ABSOLUTE (the whole allowed set, never a delta) and nullable (null = no cut). Written today by find and focus; the marquee will be its second writer, and the increment-5 regen replaces the shell-side enforcement with a real predicate inside rebuildGraph without changing this contract. Replaces the former `highlight` dimension: the search text is part of THIS value ({ids, query}), so undo restores the query and the node set together instead of leaving the search box saying one thing while the graph shows another.

_filler_note: Words a person says that the grammar does not need. Spoken English puts the noun back in ('pick first section', 'pick first card') and uses a copula ('what is this'); every one of those used to return too_many_args -- a hard error one redundant word away from a command that already worked, which is what made the first tab's items feel unreachable in Tom's 2026-07-26 review. The rescue is deliberately NARROW: it fires ONLY after a parse has already failed on arity, and NEVER on `text` or `many` verbs, so a search string (`find levin`), a tab name (`go community explorer`) or a group list (`only levin friston`) can never be silently eaten. Generic item nouns only -- no word here may also be a real group, tradition or tab name, which is why `community` is absent and `section`/`card` are safe.
_aliases_note: The SOFT layer, made hard. A conversational guide cannot require one blessed word per intent -- people say pick / select / choose / open for the same act -- but leaving that to the model means the common phrasings fail whenever the model does, which is exactly how `open the first card` died in Tom's 2026-07-26 review. Synonyms therefore resolve HERE, deterministically and under test; the model's latitude sits on TOP of this for genuinely novel phrasing, not underneath it as the only line of defence. CONTEXT-SENSITIVE where the word is genuinely ambiguous: `open levin` opens a node's article on the Sociogram, while `open first` means pick -- disambiguated by ARGUMENT SHAPE (after filler stripping), never by guessing. `when_arg_in` restricts the rewrite to those shapes; without it the alias is unconditional.

verbs._near_note: On a content tab, picking an item IS opening it. Offered ONLY where `pick` is actually in that tab's caps, so this can never advertise a verb the view lacks.

verbs._note: bare = the prose; `read details` = the provenance/metadata the speech script holds back
